identity.title: Asteroid 16 Psyche: Shape, Features, and Global Map

paper_type_evidence.quote: We develop a shape model of asteroid 16 Psyche using observations acquired in a wide range of wavelengths: Arecibo S-band delay-Doppler imaging, Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA) plane-of-sky imaging, adaptive optics (AO) images from Keck and the Very Large Telescope (VLT), and a recent stellar occultation.

A more extensive description of the observations as well as calibrations and imaging methods is given in de Kleer et al. (2021). In this paper, we use the observations primarily to constrain Psyche’s overall shape and size.

question.value: What are the refined 3D shape, dimensions, spin state, topographic features, and surface radar/optical albedo correlations of asteroid 16 Psyche, and what do they imply for its formation and composition?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we refine the size and shape of Psyche using previously published and newly obtained data sets.

We examine topographical and optical albedo features discussed in previous work [Shepard et al. 2017; Viikinkoski et al. 2018; Ferrais et al. 2020], produce a global map, and overlay it with radar albedo values, a proxy for metal concentrations in the upper meter of the regolith.
We find correlations between centers of high radar and optical albedos and discuss the consequences for these models of Psyche’s formation and structure.

analysis_steps.goal: Construct and optimize 3D shape model and spin state of Psyche

method.value: Use SHAPE software to fit 2015 Arecibo delay-Doppler images, 2015 Keck AO images, 2018-2019 VLT AO images, 22 ALMA images, and 2019 occultation silhouette sequentially from ellipsoids to spherical harmonics to a faceted vertex model (1652 vertices, 3300 facets).

evidence.quote: We utilized the SHAPE modeling software and strategies described by Magri et al. [2007b] and Shepard et al. [2017].

Once the approximate size, aspect ratios, and spin parameters are better constrained, the ellipsoids are converted into more flexible spherical harmonic shape models to flesh out the gross deviations from an ellipsoid. When these no longer improve, the best models are converted into faceted vertex models for additional fine tuning.

claims.hypothesis: Psyche is a differentiated silicate-metal world with ferrovolcanic eruptions (Johnson et al. 2020) rather than an exposed pure iron core or a randomly reaccumulated silicate-metal rubble pile.
claims.experiment: Evaluated the derived bulk density (4000 +/- 200 kg m^-3), background vs. localized radar albedos, topographic associations, and radar-optical albedo correlation against competing formation models.

claims.finding: While a porous remnant core with hypervelocity impact glass coatings cannot be completely ruled out, the preferred model is a differentiated body with an enstatite or CH/CB chondrite-like regolith and localized ferrovolcanic eruptions.

evidence.quote: Based on these findings, we cannot rule out a model of Psyche as a remnant core, but our preferred interpretation is that Psyche is a differentiated world with a regolith composition analogous to enstatite or CH/CB chondrites and peppered with localized regions of high metal concentrations. The most credible formation mechanism for these regions is ferrovolcanism as proposed by Johnson et al. [Nature Astronomy vol 4, January 2020, 41-44.].
However, of the three highest radar albedo regions, only Panthia has an associated impact structure, although we noted a possible depression at Golf.

why_this_data.value: ALMA plane-of-sky thermal emission images, high-resolution Keck/VLT AO images, and the 2019 broadside stellar occultation provide direct plane-of-sky outlines and short-integration snapshots that tightly constrain the a-, b-, and especially c-axes while mitigating rotational smearing present in radar data.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we use the observations primarily to constrain Psyche’s overall shape and size.
In addition to tightly constraining the c-axis, the 2019 occultation was effectively broadside (shape model sub-observer longitude 95°) and helped to constrain the major (a-) axis.
Second, the AO, ALMA, and occultation datasets are snap-shots of Psyche with integration times of a few seconds to a few minutes and little or no smearing.

why_this_method.value: Starting with a grid of ellipsoids before progressing to spherical harmonics and finally a faceted vertex model in SHAPE avoids local minima, while breaking radar integrations into sub-snapshots and weighting plane-of-sky snapshots at ~75% minimizes rotational smearing.

evidence.quote: When beginning the modeling process, we start with ellipsoidal models of many different sizes, aspect ratios, and spin parameters, (i.e., a grid of parameters) and find those combinations that best fit the observations. This reduces the chance of falling into a local minimum solution space.
By weighting these datasets more (~75%) than the reduced-smear delay-Doppler images (~25%) in the final model, we effectively reduced any smear to scales on the order of our image resolution.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Stripped remnant metallic core model: largely disfavored due to bulk density (~4000 kg m^-3 vs ~7900 kg m^-3 for iron) requiring >50% porosity, though cannot be completely ruled out given recent hypervelocity impact experiments on iron substrates.

evidence.quote: Based on the consensus bulk density measured for Psyche, the model of a remnant core is effectively ruled out unless it is a highly porous (~50% microporosity) object [Elkins-Tanton et al., 2020; Siltala and Granvik, 2021].
Nevertheless, given the recent experiments of high velocity impacts on metal substrates [Libourel et al. 2020], we find that our results cannot rule it out.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Ferrovolcanism on a mostly metallic body (Abrahams and Nimmo 2019): rejected as incompatible with Psyche's overall bulk density.

evidence.quote: However, the underlying assumption of this model is that Psyche is largely metallic throughout, possibly covered by a thin layer of silicate impact debris. This seems incompatible with Psyche’s overall bulk density.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Impact-gardened or reaccumulated silicate-metal rubble pile (Davis et al. 1999): considered less compelling because random reaccumulation does not explain why metal concentrations are optically bright or how impacts concentrate metal without associated craters at all radar-bright sites.

evidence.quote: If these concentrations are randomly distributed because of some reaccumulation process, it is not readily evident why they are optically brighter. If impacts are invoked, one must explain how they concentrate metal.

limitations_admitted.value: Many subtle depressions in the shape model could be noise artifacts of data processing and inversion.

evidence.quote: While there are many subtle depressions evident in our model, it is plausible that some are real, and equally plausible that some are noise artifacts.

limitations_admitted.value: Cross-hatched pattern in the ALMA images is an imaging artifact.

evidence.quote: The cross-hatched pattern visible in the data is an artifact of the imaging process.

limitations_admitted.value: Radar albedo is a whole-disk average (though weighted toward the sub-radar point within ~30-40 degrees), making the spatial map coarse and the correlation with optical albedo tentative.

evidence.quote: Given the coarse nature of a radar albedo measurement, this conclusion is necessarily tentative, but appears credible.

limitations_admitted.value: Arecibo radar is no longer available and Goldstone SNR (~15/day in 2025) is too low for future delay-Doppler imaging of Psyche.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, radar observations of Psyche at Arecibo are no longer possible. Goldstone radar can achieve SNRs of ~15/day in 2025, but these are too low for delay-Doppler imaging of Psyche.

referee_caveats_inferred: The ALMA images are treated as simple opposition plane-of-sky silhouettes in SHAPE by artificially moving the Sun to opposition, neglecting millimeter thermal inertia/beaming phase effects across the disk.
The shape inversion relies on subjective penalty weights and visual inspection to select the final vertex model among chi-square-indistinguishable solutions.

Correlation between radar and optical albedo is assessed qualitatively by visual inspection of 30 disk-integrated sub-radar points plotted over an optical map rather than a formal spatial deconvolution or statistical correlation test.

data_public_as_stated.value: VLT AO data, occultation chords, previous shape models, and the final Psyche shape model (.obj format in online supplemental materials) are publicly available via stated URLs and supplements.

evidence.quote: VLT data are from Viikinkoski et al. [2018], Ferrais et al. [2020] (https://observations.lam.fr/astero/16Psyche/).

On 2019 October 24, Psyche occulted a 10th magnitude star and a well-organized campaign led by members of the International Occultation and Timing Association (IOTA) generated 15 evenly spaced and highly accurate chords7 .
The Psyche shape file (.obj format) is included in the online supplemental materials.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~10-50 GB for raw ALMA Band 6 visibility data (88 scans); <100 MB for the processed 2D image datasets, radar echoes, and occultation chords used in SHAPE.
reproducibility.score_reason: The final 3D shape model (.obj) is released in the supplemental materials, and the ALMA project code, VLT archive URL, and occultation URLs are provided. However, reproducing the SHAPE inversion from scratch is blocked by the lack of public Arecibo delay-Doppler files, Keck AO images, and specific SHAPE penalty weights/configuration files, while the ALMA data reduction details are deferred to a companion paper.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Although the ALMA data are public and the final numeric dimensions and radar albedos are clearly stated, the core analysis is a multi-facility 3D shape inversion using SHAPE that requires non-public Arecibo delay-Doppler radar images and subjective visual model selection.
